episodes.title: Rob McConnell Interviews - MIKE KING - The Psychology of Cults
episodes.description:
Join Rob McConnell as he welcomes Mike King, internationally recognized criminal investigator, author, law enforcement veteran and specialist in criminal profiling and coercive control, for a fascinating and sometimes disturbing examination of The Psychology of Cults—how they begin, why people join them, how their leaders maintain control and what it takes for individuals to break free.With more than 40 years of experience in law enforcement, criminal investigations, intelligence and public safety, King brings an investigative perspective to one of the most complex and misunderstood aspects of human behaviour.During his 28-year law enforcement career, King served as Chief of Staff at the Utah Attorney General's Office, participated in major investigations involving violent crime and criminal organizations, and received training in behavioural analysis from FBI profilers. He also served as co-chair of the FBI's Violent Criminal Apprehension Program National Advisory Board.Today, King is widely recognized as the creator and host of Profiling Evil and Mapping Evil, true-crime platforms dedicated to examining criminal investigations, offender behaviour, missing-person cases and the techniques investigators use to uncover the truth.He is also the author of several books, including Deceived: An Investigative Memoir of the Zion Society Cult, which explores his experiences investigating a disturbing organization and the criminal conduct associated with its leadership.In this compelling conversation, Rob and Mike examine the psychological mechanisms that allow charismatic individuals to gain extraordinary influence over their followers. They explore how promises of belonging, spiritual enlightenment, personal transformation or access to exclusive knowledge can gradually develop into systems of manipulation, isolation and obedience.What makes an ordinary person vulnerable to recruitment by a high-control group?King explains how coercive leaders may exploit fundamental human needs for acceptance, certainty, purpose and community. Through carefully constructed relationships, escalating demands, emotional pressure and fear of rejection, followers can become increasingly dependent upon the very organizations that restrict their freedom.The discussion also explores some of history's most notorious cult-related tragedies and controversies, including Jonestown, Heaven's Gate, NXIVM and the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (FLDS).These cases raise unsettling questions about charismatic leadership, exploitation, psychological manipulation, abuse of authority and the difficulty of recognizing danger when it is disguised as friendship, faith or personal development.Importantly, unconventional religious or spiritual beliefs do not, by themselves, make a group abusive. The critical concerns are coercive control, exploitation, intimidation, isolation, restrictions on personal freedom and other harmful behaviours.King also examines how manipulative techniques can extend beyond religious organizations into relationships, businesses, online communities and other environments where powerful individuals seek excessive control over others.
